generatedProse.concept-context: Across the School of Sport, the three skills run as one flow each time you search. You plan the search around the question you need, build keywords such as 'small-sided games' with its synonyms, then combine and refine them in the discovery service. Running them together reaches the coaching, science and therapy studies a single word would miss.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport students need sources on whether small-sided games improve decision-making in youth players. Tom types the whole question into the service and takes the first results, with no plan and no keyword set. Amara plans first, builds keywords such as 'small-sided games' and 'youth' with synonyms, then combines and refines them with operators and a date limiter. Running the three skills as one strategy, Amara finds focused, relevant studies in less time.
generatedProse.summary: In the School of Sport, searching works best when the three skills run as one strategy. You plan around the question you need, build keywords and synonyms for each concept, then combine and refine them in the service, reusing that flow for every search. It is the whole strategy that reaches the right studies.

check.body: A student plans a search, builds keywords with synonyms, then combines and refines them in the discovery service, and finds strong sources quickly. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three skills work as one strategy: the plan, the keywords and the refined search together found good sources.
_items.feedback: Yes. Each step set up the next, and together they found strong sources.

_items.text: That only the discovery service mattered, and the plan and keywords did not.
_items.feedback: The discovery service worked because the plan and keywords prepared it. All three mattered.

_items.text: That the student was lucky, since good sources come mainly by chance.
_items.feedback: Good sources came from the strategy, not luck: plan, keywords, then a refined search.

_items.text: That planning alone was enough, and the keywords and search added nothing.
_items.feedback: Planning started it, but the keywords and the refined search did the finding too.
